newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi newspaper scolds Clinton, Dole.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi newspaper scolds Clinton, Dole.

text.p: A government-controlled newspaper on Friday hurled insults at U.S. President Bill Clinton and Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole, accusing them of escalating tension with Iraq for electoral purposes.
The official al-Iraq said both Clinton and Dole had forgotten all about America's problems, focusing instead on how to punish Iraq.

"Thus, the criminal chapter continues, threats and warnings escalate, warships and stealth bombers move as if there is nothing left for the American voter to think about but how to kill the Iraqis," the paper said in front-page editorial.
Al-Iraq said the two were like wild bulls in their race for the White House, besmirching Iraq's reputation among the American electorate.

Friday's diatribe was apparently sparked by U.S. decision to move warships and assault planes close to Iraq ready for punishing raids on Iraqi targets following Baghdad's defiance of allied planes policing no-fly zones over its territory.
Iraq has vowed to defend itself against any possible military action by the U.S. and renewed a pledge on Thursday to try to shoot allied warplanes patrolling its air space.

Life was normal in Baghdad on Friday, weekend holiday in Iraq. There were no apparent signs of a country readying itself for war. In the afternoon, tens of thousands of Moslems headed to mosques for their Friday prayers as preachers and Imams pleaded with the Almighty to punish America.

Iraq had previously reserved its ire for Clinton, whom it described as "a caged hyena" for ordering last week's cruise missile attacks on air defence targets in southern Iraq in retaliation for Baghdad's military intervention on the side of a Kurdish faction in northern Iraq.
Iraq then said the strikes were "the last kick of a dying bull (Clinton), after seeing his covert conspiracy in the Kurdish north collapse and pro-Baghdad Kurdish rebels controlling the area.
But on Friday Dole was also made part of Iraqi criticism of "ungodly Americans" and "hashish chewers" in the White House.
Republicans are heaping criticism on Clinton's Iraq policy, accusing him of not being tough enough on Baghdad.

"What is taking place between Clinton and Dole is a nasty race history has not seen before," al-Iraq said. "It shows the ugliness and stupidity of two contenders struggling for the White House at the expense of striking at the Iraqi people and committing aggression against it."
